| Year | Temporal | Individual line identity; highlighted by line emphasis for 2023 |

comments.raw_comment: In this graph, it depicts how the temperatures between the months of January and December have changed from 1850 to 2023. Generally, I noticed that as the years progress, the temperatures drastically rise. For example, in the 1940s-60s, the highest temperature between January and December was around +0.7 degrees celsius, whereas the highest temperature in 2023 was above +1.6 degrees. Each decade, the temperatures become further and further away from the average temperature of below 0 in 1850-1900. I wonder what the main cause of this rise in temperatures is and think that it may be due to climate change because greenhouse gas emissions lead to global warming. Additionally, I noticed that the temperatures for most decades are typically the highest in January, except for the 1970s and 2020s, and I wonder what the cause of this is. Also, I noticed that there is usually a drop in temperature right near December and then it rises again. This applies to my community because I have experienced global warming first hand and it is something that is very concerning for the environment. My headline for this graph would be: “How Hot Can Global Temperatures Get?”.

comments.raw_comment:
I noticed that throughout the decades, the climate of our world has only been climbing up. Despite the incredible technological advances we have seen in this decade, it looks like there has not been a stopping point for the severe increase in temperature. Additionally, I noticed how the graph depicts the heat in each decade in a different color, each decade's color becoming more red. This noticeable stylistic choice strikes me with fascination, making me ponder about the evident climate change we are witnessing.
Why hasn't there been a sense of stability in the climate already? Especially since when you look at the previous decades, the trend of the temperatures increasing has been an evident feature of today's world for a long time so it is strange that there hasn't been a sense of regulation established already. Furthermore, with the severity of the heat depicted in the 2020 decade, I wonder if the effects of that have become even more unavoidable and clear in comparison to the other decades.
Whether it is humans, animals or plants even, we are being strongly affected by the climb in climate. We have already seen the effects on air quality, endangerment of animals, and lack of snow days. If we continue our lives oblivious to the dangerous increase in temperature, this damage will be almost impossible to reverse. 
This Decade's Hot Topic

comments.raw_comment:
I noticed that each subsequent decade has relatively increased in temperature with the hottest decade since 1940 being 2020. Additionally, I noticed that in general, the decades and years didn't keep the regular seasonal pattern; the winters weren't always shown to be colder than the summers. This is especially true for the 2023 line where the temperature actually peaked in December. This is probably because of the seasonal flip between the northern and southern hemispheres. 

I wonder how much of this increase in temperature is from human activity and how much is the earth naturally increasing in temperature. Most likely, this large growth is from the peaking industrialization of the world, leading to more fossil fuel consumption and increased greenhouse gas release. I also wonder what could happen in the future if this trend were to continue. Would we find a solution before the earth became completely uninhabitable or insupportable to our current way of life? 

This affects my community and the whole world because if temperatures keep rising, eventually life itself will need to make a major change or risk extinction. This problem is also not isolated to the distant future because, even if the world does not completely end due to the rise in temperature, it will see a substantial shift for the worse, for example, increasing natural disasters and worse air quality.

The average global temperature has been increasing rapidly, with each year becoming hotter than the last. The average global temperature is swiftly increasing, meaning we aren’t doing enough to stop or even delay global warming. This graph goes to show that if we can’t come together to enact change now, there will never be a good time. It only will get harder and harder to end global warming, and the point of no return for our Earth is rapidly approaching.

comments.raw_comment: In the graph, I noticed that the global temperature increases every decade. However, in 2023 in particular, the temperature shoots upwards in December to above +1.6 degrees celsius out of the general “grouped” temperature in the 2020s. I also noticed that in each decade, typically, January possesses a high outlier temperature (but this is different in the 2020s and the 1970s). I wonder why the 1940s-60s and 1970s average temperatures are nearly the same (with a slight increase in the 1970s). I also wonder how climate change directly affects the average temperatures in the graph, particularly with the abnormally high temperatures for 2023. I am curious if the temperatures will fall back down into the “oscillation” pattern in 2024, or will they continue to rise? comments.raw_comment:
I notice that average temperature of the Earth has risen drastically since the 1940s. I notice that from 1940-1970 the average temperature only slightly increased. With a maxiumum of a .8 degrees Celsius increase. However, from 1990 to 2023 the average temperature drastically increased.  The maximum increase was over 1.6 degrees Celsius. Both of these increases in temperature occurred over a 30 year period of time. Although they occurred over the same period of time they were drastically different, as the Earth has heated up significantly in the past decade. I also notice that 2023 was the hottest year ever. I wonder if the immense damage that humans have inflicted upon the Earth can be reversed as much as it needs to be. I wonder if people are too stubborn to make the changes that need to be made to salvage the Earth for future generations. As a result of this I wonder if the Earth's temperature will just continue and continue to increase until life as we know it is completely altered to the point of no return. This relates to myself and my community as I have seen the Earth getting hotter. This has been a relatively warm winter with days in the high 50s and 60s. There has been very little snow and only a few frigid days. I often wonder what the winters will be like as I grow older and if I will ever experience another winter like those that I experienced as a child.


Temperature Turmoil

This graph shows temperatures throughout the past few decades (1940s-2023). The trend is each decade, temperatures are rising. The average temperature for 1850-1900 has risen 1°C since then. Temperatures in the 20s have not been exceptionally high on a global scale. This may be due to COVID and the COVID recovery years (2021-2022) because it halted many modes of transportation and slowed the economy due to a reduction in manufacturing. These factors can play a role in reducing the temperatures of the world. As we know, fossil fuels produced from transportation and manufacturing are depleting the ozone layer and causing temperatures to rise (global warming). During COVID, studies showed that the ozone layer was healing itself as a result of less carbon emissions going into the air. In 2023, the world was back in full swing. The carbon emissions probably depleted every ounce the ozone layer supposedly healed during COVID following when the restrictions were lifted. In 2023 the ozone layer probably broke down even further resulting in a rise in temperatures. I wonder why temperatures were so high in 2016. This relates to me because it is the dead of winter in NJ and this Saturday is going to be 57° Fahrenheit! This is abnormally high for a winter day in the middle of February. I predict that in future years, temperatures will continue to rise. If we do not do something major to help reduce global warming soon there will be dire consequences. 
"2023 Record High, We Might Die"

All years follow a certain pattern in which at the start of January the temperature richest at’s highest point, then drops, and in December it goes back up again. Before 2023, 2016 was the year with the highest temperature, but 2023 surpassed it. 2023 seems to be a weird year, as the temperature stayed comparatively low at the start of the year, and then it steadily increased and reached its highest point in December. 
I wonder what was different about 2023 than other years for it to become such a strange year?
This affects me and my community because we can directly feel the impact of it. The winter’s shorter, the summers seem hotter, and the wildlife is being affected by it. Also, as a Hondurian, the effects of climate change in Honduras are concerning as many cities are flooded more frequently and the heat is worse than before even as a tropical country.

comments.raw_comment: This graph depicts the rising average temperatures per decade. Global warming and climate change have become the forefront issues for the World's health, so I imagine the sudden change can be attributed to the massive increase of waste and trash that has been accumulating the last century coming to fruition. This is an important issue because it relates to every human. I remember when there would be blizzards in October and now it is lucky if we get snow by February. I have noticed the effects of global warming in my daily life now, especially in the last few years. The effects of climate change affect every part of nature, hence why it is important to notice, acknowledge, and fix global warming. A possible headline could be "Lets Turn Down the Thermostat and Take a Look at Global Warming"

comments.raw_comment:
This graph depicts the increase in temperature recorded from the 1940s to 2023. From the decades recorded, it can be seen that temperatures started to steadily increase around the end of the 1970s going into the 1980s. After such, temperatures appear to climb higher and higher each decade. This leads up to 2023 being the hottest year recorded on the graph. Even though each bar indicating a temperature rise only differs in +0.2°C, these small increases are linked to grave impacts on the climate of the world. I wonder why 2016 had the most major spike in the 2010s. I understand during this year the Arctic regions experienced uncharacteristic heat and that, globally, oceans were reported to have higher temperatures than normal, resulting in international panic. I also wonder if some of this heat was normal due to natural intervals of the earth heating, but it was untimely coupled with external factors caused by society. This relates to my community because climate change is a major issue. Climate change affects everything from air quality to food. In my local community, there is a strong Environmental Commission that strives to improve the quality of the land and ultimately find ways to rally people together and fight back against climate change. No matter where you live, the negative impacts of climate change trickle in and affect all of us, even in minor ways. 

“Is It Hot In Here or Is It Just Climate Change in 2023?”

Whether that’s more recycling, use of electric vehicles, other forms of green energy, etc, working on a community and individual level is all we can do. If enough communities can do that, change will be seen.

I notice two trends on the graph: first, the average temperature increases by about .2 degrees Celsius every decade; second, the range of temperatures on average increases every decade. The exceptions to this trend are the 1970s where the average temperature does not change significantly from the previous decade, and the 1980s where the range of temperatures is significantly smaller than the 1940s-1970s.

Global warming relates to my community for numerous reasons but one of the most notable are potholes. The toll wide temperature ranges have on infrastructure is obvious. Looking at this graph from a modern perspective, the response will automatically be global warming. The world is warming, that is a fact. However, what’s causing it? In the 1940s-1970s the temperatures remained fairly constant. But, this was the era of large industrialization, planes and automobiles. For the first time, the average citizen had a car. So, why has the increase in temperature been so significant in modern times? Times that people are so very conscious of carbon emissions? If the argument is that climate change is caused by cars (hence the need for electric cars), then why would an era with such a focus on automobiles have such a low temperature? Were the emissions not happening? Do the emissions accumulate? If they accumulate, then why was the temperature seemingly not impacted by the emissions of the Industrial Revolution? What do you notice?
I notice that there has been a steady increase in temperatures each decade from the 1940s to the 2020s. Some people believe that global warming is fake, but the data clearly shows that temps have been on the rise.

According to the EUCCCS, since the 1960s Earth’s average temperature has steadily increased each year. At the start of 2023, the average temperature was at an all time high, with the high and low January temperatures being close to 1.8 and 1.05 degrees above the average temperature in 1960, respectively.  Between 1940 and 1960 the temperatures followed very similar trends - almost indistinguishable from each other - which makes me wonder what happened in the 1970s to cause such a spike in temperatures. In the 1970s, oil production was at an all time high and America began the steep climb of industrialization, helped by the development of steam powered vehicles. However, this was only in America. What happened in the rest of the world to spike such change in Global temperatures? An increase in global temperature is detrimental to life all over the world. Since many plants and animals are not accustomed to these changed temperatures, they will be forced to adapt or die off. Thus, if global temperatures continue along their current trend, much of life may not be able to persist in the future, affecting all future generations. Furthermore, intense heat in arid climates will dry out the soil, making it infertile to farming and therefore taking away possible food sources. Our current generation’s grandchildren and possibly even children will not be able to experience the beauty of Earth as we have.

1. Mean global temperature has been rising by nearly a fifth of a degree every decade since the 1970s. With this change in average temperature comes an increase in variation as well. These changes all amounted to 2023 being the warmest year on record, and by a lot. If this trend continues we will reach the warned +2 degrees celsius sooner than many people realize. 

2. I wonder why temperature didn’t have nearly as much change before the 1970s. The change seemed to happen very quickly as well which I find to be strange when talking about rising global temperatures. I also wonder why 2023’s average temperature started increasing so far before other years that allowed it to become the hottest year by such a large margin. Finally, I wonder whether the large increase in temperature stems from human actions, or if it is naturally occurring. 

3. Climate change is something that relates to my community and all other communities around the globe. Changing temperatures pose threats to much of the wildlife and activities that me and my friends love to do. I even notice now that we get less snow each year for skiing, one of my favorite things to do in the winter. While I think increasing temperatures are already prevalent in my community, it will only increase in prevalence as temperatures become more extreme. 

4. Rapidly Increasing Temperatures: Naturally Occurring or Human Actions?

comments.raw_comment:
What do you notice?
There is a clear upward trend in temperature throughout the decades. However, I also noticed that the title is a bit misleading. It uses the word "shattered", which immediately makes me think there was a huge surge in temperature. After looking at the graph, the average was only a measly 0.1 degrees Celsius more.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why there is an increase in temperature over time. Did humans cause it? Is it a natural cycle of the Earth? My guess, because there is a very minimal change in temperature through decades, is that this is a natural cycle of the Earth.

How does this relate to you and your community?
Realistically, this doesn't bother or relate to me much. Yes, there is a slow increase of about a Celsius in temperature. However, it is not large enough of an increase for me to feel it physically or worry about it at all. To summarize, this doesn't relate to me or my community enough to say anything definitive.
